source.title: Reason to Rote: Rethinking Memorization in Reasoning
source.authors: Yu-Pei Du; Philipp Mondorf; Silvia Casola; Yue-Kun Yao; Robert Litschko; Barbara Plank

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains small transformer language models from scratch on synthetic reasoning tasks with randomly corrupted labels, then measures memorization and generalization. This tests label-noise memorization conceptually, but not the original image-classification recipe.
record.gate_note: The study reports results on noisy training labels and clean validation examples. It does not test completely random labels on image datasets, shuffled or Gaussian inputs, explicit regularization, or the cited original recipes. Cited results from other work are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests learning order (V6) and low-noise training fit and generalization (parts of V4) in transformers trained from scratch on synthetic reasoning tasks. It does not test completely random labeling (V1).
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: in the tested synthetic tasks, noisy-label memorization retains and relies on reasoning mechanisms, uses distributed encodings, and in FDA involves outlier heuristics in higher-layer MLP activations.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains decoder-only transformer language models from scratch on synthetic four-digit addition and two-hop reasoning, with a small fraction of corrupted training labels. It does not reproduce image-classification experiments or their original settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Task and model size affect performance: THR requires a larger model, and the 4-layer, 256-hidden-size THR model reaches 68% validation accuracy at 10% noise. Noise rate was varied only over low values.

fits_no_version.finding: Correct labels are recoverable in intermediate layers before corrupted labels dominate later layers, including in reinitialized Qwen2.5-0.5B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reasoning computations persist within trained models that output memorized noisy labels.

fits_no_version.finding: Providing the correct first FDA answer digit enables nearly perfect generation of the remaining correct digits.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A correct answer prefix can recover reasoning output on memorized noisy examples.

fits_no_version.finding: Bridge-entity removal, head ablation, and activation patching reveal shared reasoning dependencies, distributed memories, and outlier heuristics.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Low-noise memorization reuses and modifies reasoning computations in these trained transformers.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The authors note that the study focuses on relatively small models trained from scratch and uses synthetic datasets. Several mechanistic results are described qualitatively with figure values not given in prose. Noise rates are low and do not test fully random labels.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported result-bearing conditions omitted. Figure-only numeric values were not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, near-zero training error on that labeling, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters relative to true-label training.
Training-time ratio relative to true labels and convergence slowing with increasing corruption.
The sweep from zero to complete corruption and steady test-error growth toward chance. FDA full-answer training fit is not established by the first-token accuracy measure.
Controlled effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation, including generalization after removing them.
Learning order under completely random labeling and outside the tested synthetic reasoning settings.

missing.what: FDA model with 8 layers and hidden dimension 128 cannot memorize all noisy training instances, whereas the 4-layer, 256-hidden model achieves perfect memorization. Record the incomplete-fit condition and identify its noise rates if readable.
THR model with 4 layers and hidden dimension 256 achieves 68% validation accuracy at 10% noise; the authors state that its validation performance worsens as noise increases.
Near-perfect final Train-Clean accuracy is explicitly reported for both main models. These clean-training measurements are needed alongside Mem-Noisy to substantiate overall training fit.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Missing experimental coverage does not warrant limits_scope labels. Layer order is distinct from training order, and THR's imperfect early corrected-label accuracy does not challenge V6. The supplied text also inconsistently describes the pre-memorization checkpoint as step 1,000 with approximately 100% corrected-label accuracy versus approximately 100% by step 4,000 in Section 3.1.

versions.untested_parts: Image datasets; completely random labeling of the entire training set; test error at chance; original architectures and optimizer hyperparameters.
Noise rates span only 2%, 5%, and 10% for FDA, and 5% and 10% for THR; not a sweep to fully random labels. Test error rising steadily toward chance is not reported.
The models are trained from scratch on synthetic reasoning tasks, not the original deep-network image settings.

rows.subject: FDA model (4 layers, 256 hidden size, 4 attention heads)
rows.operation_detail: Train on four-digit addition with 5% of training labels replaced by random sums.
rows.note: The authors report near-perfect final accuracy on Mem-Noisy; no exact endpoint percentage is given in the prose.
rows.check: Only 5% of labels are corrupted, so this does not test V1. FDA accuracy measures the first answer digit, not exact full-answer accuracy.

rows.subject: FDA model (4 layers, 256 hidden size, 4 attention heads)
rows.operation_detail: Measure accuracy on noisy training inputs with their unobserved correct labels during later training.
rows.note: The paper describes the onset of memorization after early learning of the correct labels.
rows.check: The decline after step 5,000 coincides with increasing Mem-Noisy accuracy, directly supporting later noise memorization. A decline here is not an incomplete V6 effect.

rows.note: The paper reports that the model eventually memorizes noisy labels; it does not give an exact endpoint percentage in the text.
rows.check: Only 5% of labels are corrupted; this does not test V1.

rows.subject: FDA model (4 layers, 256 hidden size, 4 attention heads)
rows.operation_detail: Train FDA models while varying the label noise rate.
rows.note: The appendix says the chosen model achieves perfect memorization accuracy and reports similar trends across settings; figure values are not reconstructed.
rows.check: Low corruption rates do not test V1. FDA memorization accuracy concerns the first answer digit; exact endpoints for each noise rate are not supplied in the readable figure text.

rows.subject: FDA model (4 layers, 256 hidden size, 4 attention heads)
rows.operation_detail: Train FDA models while varying the label noise rate.
rows.note: The appendix discusses model-size and noise-rate effects, but supplies no textual exact values for this condition.
rows.check: The supplied figure text does not establish whether validation error rises steadily across 2%, 5%, and 10% noise. This does not test V1.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-0.5B
rows.operation_detail: Train on FDA with 5% noise and inspect logit-lens predictions across layers.
rows.measure: Logit-lens prediction of the correct label on noisy training instances
rows.value: computes the correct label in early layers, then overwrites it with the memorized corrupted label in later layers
rows.note: The text reports the two-stage pattern; no exact layer accuracies are stated in prose.
rows.check: Early versus late layers in a trained model are not early versus late training. This logit-lens result tests neither V6 learning order nor V1 completely random labeling.

rows.subject: FDA model (4 layers, 256 hidden size, 4 attention heads)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate generation after appending the correct first answer digit to a noisy training prompt.
rows.measure: Accuracy of remaining generated addition digits
rows.note: This is conditional generation after supplying the correct first answer token, not unprompted full-answer fitting.
rows.check: Generation after supplying the correct first digit measures conditional recovery of reasoning, not any listed claim version.

rows.subject: THR model (8 layers, 256 hidden size, 4 attention heads)
rows.operation_detail: Remove linearly detectable bridge-entity signals with INLP and patch modified residual streams at inference.
rows.measure: Average prediction probability for the noisy answer token
rows.baseline: random and mean null-space baselines; exact values not stated
rows.value: removing bridge entities substantially harms memorization; impact milder than on clean validation
rows.note: This mechanistic intervention bears on noisy-label memorization, but the paper does not give exact probability values in the prose.
rows.check: An inference-time intervention on bridge representations measures causal dependence of memorization, not training fit or learning order.

rows.subject: THR model (8 layers, 256 hidden size, 4 attention heads)
rows.operation_detail: Ablate selected attention heads by forcing each token to attend only to itself.

conditions.value: L0H3, L1H2 and L1H3 together, L2H1

rows.measure: Faithfulness of memorization of noisy labels
rows.value: more mildly affected than generalization faithfulness
rows.note: The text gives a comparative qualitative result; the plotted faithfulness values are not transcribed.
rows.check: Attention-ablation faithfulness measures mechanism dependence, not a listed version. The prose identifies L0H3, whereas Figure 5b labels the corresponding head L0H0; this source inconsistency should be retained.

rows.subject: FDA model (4 layers, 256 hidden size, 4 attention heads)
rows.operation_detail: Ablate selected layer-0 attention heads by forcing each token to attend only to itself.

conditions.value: L0H1 and L0H3; L0H2 and L0H4

rows.measure: Faithfulness of memorization of noisy labels
rows.value: smaller impact for L0H1 and L0H3 ablation; comparable drop for L0H2 and L0H4 ablation
rows.note: Qualitative prose describes two distinct head-group outcomes; plotted values are not transcribed.
rows.check: Ablation faithfulness does not measure a listed version. The prose names L0H4 despite four heads, while Figure 5c labels heads L0H0–L0H3; head identities require clarification.

rows.subject: FDA model (4 layers, 256 hidden size, 4 attention heads)
rows.operation_detail: Replace post-memorization MLP activations with pre-memorization activations.
rows.baseline: post-memorization model without activation patching; exact value not stated
rows.note: The paper reports a strong reduction in faithfulness, but does not give an exact value in the prose.
rows.check: Replacing activations at inference measures a mechanism intervention, not spontaneous training dynamics or completely random-label fitting.

rows.subject: FDA model (4 layers, 256 hidden size, 4 attention heads)
rows.operation_detail: Replace post-memorization MLP activations with pre-memorization activations.
rows.baseline: post-memorization model without activation patching; exact value not stated
rows.value: only slightly affects validation faithfulness; validation accuracy is restored to 100%
rows.note: The text explicitly reports the validation outcome of this intervention.
rows.check: Validation recovery under activation patching does not test any listed version. FDA accuracy concerns the first answer digit.

rows.subject: FDA model (4 layers, 256 hidden size, 4 attention heads)
rows.operation_detail: Replace post-memorization MLP activations with those from a random noisy instance.
rows.measure: Faithfulness drop for memorization and generalization
rows.baseline: post-memorization model without activation patching; exact value not stated
rows.value: only mild drops in faithfulness for both mechanisms
rows.note: Random activation patching is explicitly used as a control.
rows.check: This is a mechanistic patching control, not evidence for any listed version.
